text:
Predicates:
Allowed(x, y) ::: Pets are allowed in building x.
DepositRequired(x) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in building x.
SecurityDeposit(x, y) ::: The security deposit for building x is y.
MonthlyRent(x, y) ::: The monthly rent for building x is y.
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
Cat(x) ::: x is a cat.
ManagedBuilding(x) ::: x is a managed building.
Premises:
∃x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ Allowed(x, pet)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → DepositRequired(x)) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → (SecurityDeposit(x, y) ↔ (y = monthRent(x) ∨ y > monthRent(x)))) ::: The security deposit can be either equal to one month's rent or more.
Cat(fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat.
∀x (Cat(x) → Pet(x)) ::: Cats are pets.
ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
MonthlyRent(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
∀x (Rent(x) ↔ (Allowed(x, fluffy) ∧ SecurityDeposit(x, y) ≤ 1500)) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
2000 > 1500 ::: 2000$ is more than $1500.
Conclusion:
SecurityDeposit(oliveGarden, y) ↔ (y = 2000 ∨ y > 2000) ::: The security deposit at the Olive Garden is either $2000 or more.
